evidence: Right side: a pyramidal roof with a finial emerges from the tops of the pine grove, its eave outline clear; only several vertical fine lines of the building itself are seen, the rest hidden behind the woodland. | Lower right: pine branches and needle clusters press diagonally over the lower part and sides of the building in front, forming a layered effect of seeing the building behind the grove, half hidden and half exposed. | Center to left: several steep peak rocks stand in cloud mist, and on the left rippling lines spread out flat; the built element stands alone among the trees at the right edge, not directly adjoining the peaks.
distinction: The building is brought into the scene chiefly through the concealment-and-revelation relation of an exposed roof and a building body pressed over by the pine grove, rather than corresponding to the peaks or a water gap to mark out a single scenic spot.

evidence: Center-lower part: beneath the dense shade of a large tree is a thatched cottage, inside which a person sits upright; to the right of the house a fence encloses it, and on the open ground outside the fence two people stand facing the house, in the posture of paying a visit | Left end: a plank bridge spans between the stream banks, connecting the sloping ground on either side and forming a passable movement clue | Right side to lower right: a pale-colored path winds down along the valley toward the open ground before the house; at the lower-right corner another trace of a bridge is seen, connecting with the direction in which the figures before the house are moving
distinction: Although the house is covered by tree shade, its body and eave columns are openly and recognizably exposed, and concealment and revelation are not the main way of signaling the built presence; the painting connects to the area before the house by bridge, path, and moving figures, presenting a spatial process of approaching the built elements, so C4 is chosen.

evidence: Center-right: an open veranda is elevated on multiple columns above the rocks of the stream bank, its platform and railing extending horizontally along the water, the column feet landing according to the rise and fall of the rocks, the site corresponding to the bank's configuration | Upper middle: pine canopies slant down over the veranda, the roof ridge and tile surfaces partly hidden among pine needles, the eaves emerging from beneath the pine shade | Left side to right bank: a group of scholars sits on flat rocks and terraces of the rocky slope, while attendants to the right work among the rock platforms, figures and built elements alike distributed along the rocks of the stream bank
distinction: Although the pine branches covering the roof create concealment and revelation, the front of the building itself is fully open and exposed, and the built presence does not rely on an exposed roof to be signaled; the more dominant relation is that the veranda body is placed on elevated column feet according to the rocks of the stream bank and unfolds along the water, with terrain directly participating in the layout of the site

evidence: Lower left: a railed diagonal ramp rises from the foreground ground and joins the terrace entrance of the walled courtyard on the left, forming a passage from outside to inside | Center to central courtyard: a low-railed path crosses the flower beds, skirts the Taihu rocks, and extends to the central courtyard, then links by steps and railing posts to the gallery beneath the open veranda on the right | On the central courtyard path: a maid carrying objects walks along the courtyard path, a fan-holder stands beside the path, and a stooping figure is at the path's end; the figures distributed along the path suggest a process of continued touring
distinction: Although the weeping willows brushing the eaves cause local screening, the ramp, paths, and steps link the built elements on left and right, with figures moving along them; the process of entry and arrival runs through the composition more than the layering of concealment and revelation

evidence: Lower left: water ripples and bank rocks form a stream bank, and the sloping ground rises from the bank toward the center, forming a site layering of bank and slope meeting | Center: on the open slope surface several beasts are scattered according to the high and low of the slope, the slope top joining the great rock above and the pendent pine branches | Right side and above: a large tree trunk slants out from the upper right, and a rock face hangs down from above, enclosing with the slope an unfolded space; no traces of built elements such as buildings, walls, bridges, or paths are seen anywhere in the painting
distinction: The organizing role of the terrace and shoreline in the distribution of objects runs through the painting and is closer to the visible spatial relations than the local screening of trees and rocks, but both are weak in evidence owing to the absence of built elements

evidence: Middle of the left edge: an arc-shaped raised object is cut off by the painting's edge, exposing only its curved outline and fine line patterns; it cannot be reliably identified as a building, bridge, or boat shelter | Lower middle to center: several large trees grow from the foreground sloping rocks, their trunks and branches covering the middle ground, with a herd boy and ox exposed among the trunks and beneath the canopy, forming a layered effect of front-to-back screening and exposure | Middle-ground horizontal band: open water or flat open country runs across the painting, the far bank low and faintly receding, with figures and cattle distributed on the grass at the bank's edge; no clear houses, walls, or terrace bases are seen
distinction: The painting's layering is organized mainly by the foreground trees and rocks screening and exposing the middle-ground scenery, while it lacks enterable clues such as bridges, paths, or gates and any destination for movement, so the screening layering is closer to the visible relations than movement into the landscape

evidence: Center-left to lower center: a row of buildings with railings and densely packed column feet is elevated at the water's edge of a sloping bank, the roof surfaces extending horizontally along the shoreline | Center of the painting: multiple roof tiers step down and up with the slope, rising level by level from the water's edge up the slope, the layout corresponding to the undulations of the terraces | Center-right: a large-roofed house sits on a terrace, the lower half of its building body screened by the large foreground tree, exposing only the roof and part of the walls and windows
distinction: Although the building on the right is locally screened by the canopy, the dominant relation running through the middle section is the terrain-responsive placement of column feet elevated and roofs unfolding with the height of the sloping bank; concealment and revelation are only a local effect

evidence: Lower left: a staff-bearing figure stands between the pine trunk and the sloping rocks, his body turned toward the open space to the right, in a posture of standing or about to set out | Lower middle to right: a pale-ink bank line slants from the lower-left sloping rocks toward the right, penetrating the large area of unpainted space, with sparse small grasses dotting the bank's edge, suggesting a passable extension along the bank | Upper left to center: several pine trunks slant out from the upper left, pine branches hanging over the upper part of the painting, beneath which is the only solid ground where the sloping rocks and figure are located; the rest of the painting is unpainted space
distinction: The only discernible spatial organization in the painting is the staff-bearing figure and the movement extension suggested by the bank line, rather than any built site placed according to terrain, so it is assigned under the closest category, C4, rather than C1

evidence: Center-right: a line of walking figures is arranged one after another upward along a slope gap in a mountain hollow, forming a marching sequence that turns from the valley floor into the depths | Among the pines at center right: where the pine branches half screen it, there is a horizontally placed frame-like or house-like structure, partly screened by trunks and branches; it cannot be reliably identified as a built element | Center-left valley floor: a wheeled carriage, horses, and staff-bearing attendants stop on the flat slope, connecting front to back with the uphill file at the upper right, suggesting a relation of continued movement
distinction: The painting organizes space by the marching sequence of the group ascending the slope gap and turning into the mountain hollow, with the suspected structure deep within that sequence, rather than merely forming layers through screening by the pine grove, so C4 is closer to the visible relations than C2.

evidence: Center-right hilltop: a pavilion building emerges, body and roof, from behind the top of a rounded hill, its site hidden by the hill, beside it a withered tree and a red-leaved tree | Center-right water's edge: the roofs and walls of several buildings emerge from between the trunks of foreground withered trees, trees in front and buildings behind, forming a layered effect of seeing buildings through trees | Lower-right slope foot: a building is half hidden behind sloping rocks and groves, exposing only its roof and part of its walls, its waterside side remaining open
distinction: The built elements are mostly brought into the scene by roofs and walls emerging from among the trees and from behind slopes; the layering of concealment and revelation runs through the painting more than the correspondence of sites placed with the sloping bank

evidence: Right side: beneath layered cliffs is a gentle terrace whose front edge directly adjoins the water, forming a clear configuration of a waterside platform | Middle-ground horizontal band: islets and sloping banks spread horizontally along the water, groves distributed in bands at the slope tops and shoreline, and the relation between the shoreline and the slope foot is discernible | Whole work: no built elements or movement clues such as buildings, walls and eaves, bridges, paths, or gates are seen; the foreground is open water and unpainted space
distinction: The visible organization is the placement framework formed by the terrace and the configuration following the bank, whereas the roof and eave concealment and revelation required by C2 is entirely absent from the painting

evidence: Lower left to lower center: a gentle slope slants from lower left toward lower right, rows of grass distributed at the slope foot, and on the slope surface stands a white sheep with its head lowered; no buildings, walls, bridges, or paths are seen anywhere in the work. | Upper left: pine-willow-like branches hang in from outside the painting, covering above the slope surface, with a large area of unpainted space between them and the slope surface, and no building outlines. | Center-right slope edge: thorny brambles and bamboo branches slant out through gaps at the slope edge, their twig lines interwoven, but neither where they screen nor behind the branches are there any traces of built elements.
distinction: The only spatial organization running through the painting is the slope's configuration, with grasses, thorns, and animals all distributed according to the slope surface and edge, closer to the logic of terrain-responsive placement; an explanation by concealment and revelation requires buildings exposed by screening foliage, and there are no built elements in the painting to be exposed.

evidence: Lower left: withered branches and groves with red and white dotted leaves overlap front and back, and a dark-ink dotted-leaf grove screens behind them; no traces of built elements such as roofs or walls are seen among the groves | Middle of the left edge: a horizontal band of mist or distant trees cuts off the groves on the left, forming a layer of blocking and revealing, within which there are no building outlines | Lower right: blue-green colored twin peaks and, behind them, a gray solitary rock rise before a large area of unpainted space; at the peaks and slope foot there are no pavilions, paths, or ferries
distinction: Given the absence of built elements, the only organizing device running through the painting is the layer of blocking and concealment and revelation formed by groves and mist bands, which is closer to the visible relations than focal scenic accentuation relying solely on the rising of solitary peaks

evidence: Center-left: only the head of a rat-shaped animal emerges from behind a large clump of foliage, its body screened by the leaves, forming a clear layer of concealment and revelation | Center: a gourd is half covered by overlapping large leaves on all sides, a flowering branch extending through a gap in the leaves, the foliage forming a front-to-back screening relation | Lower middle to the whole work: a lightly washed earthen slope runs across the painting, with chrysanthemum clusters, thorns, and gourd vines distributed on it, and in front of the slope an open space where a weasel-shaped animal walks; no traces of built elements such as buildings, bridges, paths, or gates are seen anywhere in the painting
distinction: The most prominent spatial organization in the painting is the layering formed by foliage screening and revealing, rather than the correspondence of object sites with the slope's configuration, so the concealment-and-revelation mechanism is chosen rather than the terrain-responsive mechanism

evidence: Lower right to lower center: the sloping rocky bank rises from the water's edge, pines and withered trees standing at the slope top and amid the rocks, their trunks and branches stretching toward the water on the left; no traces of built elements such as buildings, walls, bridges, or paths are seen between the bank and the rocks. | Upper left to upper middle: a low flat sandbar and distant mountains rendered in pale ink spread horizontally along the water's edge, the shoreline gentle, with rows of clustered trees dotting the ridges. | Center: a large area of unpainted water separates the near sloping bank from the distant sandbar, forming an open and unenclosed plane; the water has no connecting clues such as boats, bridges, or fords.
distinction: The visible organization consists mainly of the participation of the bank and waterside terrain in the placement of trees and shoreline, running through the near and the distant ground; the concealment and revelation of trees and rocks screening one another is confined to within the near-ground tree group and plays a weaker organizing role.

evidence: Lower-right waterside: an elongated building is elevated at the water, columns supporting its building body visible beneath it at the bank's edge, the building extending horizontally along the waterside | On the slope at the lower-right corner: another building sits on slightly higher sloping ground above and to the right of the waterside building, a seated figure visible inside, the two buildings placed according to the high and low of the sloping bank | Lower-right sloping bank: the building group backs onto the sloping bank and pine grove, facing the open water to the left and the central great rock and waterfall, its sites laid out with the turning of the shoreline
distinction: The building sites and their elevation directly follow the waterside and sloping ground (elevated at the water, placed separately along the slope), whereas tree cover reaches only part of the building bodies, and the layering of concealment and revelation is less evident than the relation of terrain participating in the placement

evidence: Upper half: between the cliffs hanging down from the upper edge of the painting, several groups of groves hang, their branches and leaves half screened before and behind the cliff faces, forming a layer of screening and revealing, the cliff feet ending at the unpainted space in the middle | Lower left: the grove behind the sloping rocks exposes only the crown, its trunk and roots blocked by the rock mass, presenting a front-to-back layer of concealment and revelation behind the rock | Middle to lower part: the middle is a large area of unpainted space, below is a rock face with vertical texture strokes and a grove at the lower right; no recognizable built elements or movement clues such as buildings, eaves, walls, bridges, or paths are seen anywhere in the painting
distinction: The visible organization in the painting is mainly the layer of screening and revealing of mountain rocks and woodland, while enterable clues such as bridges, paths, gates, or fords required by C4 are entirely invisible in the painting, so assigning it to C2 under the concealment-and-revelation structure is closer to the visible relations

evidence: Lower middle: a low flat bridge spans the stream ravine, its left end joining the foreground sloping rocky stream bank and its right end joining the flat ground before the building group on the right bank, forming a connection for crossing the stream and reaching the buildings | Lower right to center right: several groups of buildings and veranda galleries are distributed along the right bank of the stream valley from near to far, their building bodies, lattice windows, and elevated terrace bases clearly recognizable and directly linked with the bank ground at the bridge end | Center: the stream valley before the bridge is an open earthen-colored clearing extending deep into the middle of the painting, and the building group is laid out along the turning of the valley, suggesting that after crossing the bridge one may continue deeper
distinction: The bridge and the valley clearing provide the movement process of crossing the stream to approach the building group and turning into the valley; the access clue organizes the lower half of the composition; the waterside, platform-based placement of the buildings is only a background condition and does not play a dominant organizing role

evidence: Below, from lower left to lower right: a flat terrace unfolds beside unpainted water, its edge outlined in ink with turns and slope foot, forming the base that carries activity in the lower part of the painting | Lower left: several attendant figures holding staffs and fans stand gathered on the terrace, close against the thick pine trunk at the left edge, their standing place corresponding to the terrace's edge | Middle to upper part: a great peak occupies the top, pine branches slant out from the left bank and run across the middle of the painting, their tips hanging over above the terrace, which lies beneath the force of the peaks and the screening of the pines
distinction: The bearing and correspondence of the lower terrace and shoreline to the site are clearer and more sustained through the painting than the access and movement clues, so it is assigned to the terrain-responsive placement category rather than access to secluded settings.

evidence: Lower center-right: an open pavilion stands on a stone-revetted terrace platform at the water's edge; the platform follows the bank slope, and steps in front of it descend with the slope to connect to the bank. The open face of the building itself faces the wide water surface and distant mountains to the left | Lower left: a waterside landing platform is set at a low point of the bank slope, on which a figure bends over the water in operation; the platform edge reaches the water directly, forming a high-low division along the bank with the pavilion terrace above | Around and behind the pavilion: pine branches from the right extend and overlap the right edge of the roof; a willow grove is dense behind the pavilion, but the columned gallery, the figure on the couch, and the terrace base are all fully exposed
distinction: Trees only overlap the roof at its edge; the building itself and the terrace base are entirely exposed; the dominant relationship is that the terrace base and steps are placed following the waterside slope, not a composition formed through concealment and revelation

evidence: Lower right: a bridge with balustrades crosses a stream gully; its left end connects to the stream-bank slope where the thatched hall is located, forming an entry cue for approaching the built structure across the stream | Lower center: a pyramidal-roofed thatched hall stands by the stream on a slope amid woodland at the valley mouth, adjacent to the bridge and bank, serving as the arrival point of the movement sequence | Middle-left valley to the upper mountain hollow: the stream valley runs through from bottom to top; a walker stands in the valley, and above him village houses on the slope hollow and a small hut in the higher mountain hollow are distributed in turn, presenting an extension of tracing the valley into the depths
distinction: The bridge, the walker, and the through-running stream valley string together the thatched hall, the village, and the hollow-mouth hut into a sequence that can be reached and continued upward, and this organizing role runs through the whole painting; C1 only states that each built structure is sited in place and fails to cover the linkage between the bridge and the movement cues.

evidence: Middle-right lower: a thatch-roofed open pavilion is supported over the water by a row of wooden posts; the platform and railings project beyond the bank, the rear of the building closely abuts the foot of the cliff slope, and the base height follows the turns of the shoreline | Middle of the painting: the left section of the building is partly screened by foreground blue-green rocks and pine branches, the roof emerging from behind the rocks, but the open pavilion, figures, and posts are wholly exposed above the water | Lower-left bank edge: scattered rocks at the slope foot extend along the shoreline to the building base, and a boy on the bank bends over among the rocks, showing the building is sited at the junction of the slope foot and the waterside
distinction: The building is raised over the water on posts with its back to the cliff foot, and the correspondence between its siting and the terrain and waterside runs through the main subject; rock screening reaches only one corner of the building itself, and concealment does not constitute a dominant layer

evidence: Upper left: the roof, eaves, and upper edge of the terrace base of a hall emerge above curly cloud patterns; the base and lower part are obscured by cloud, and a small roof to the left is half-hidden at the cloud edge | Center: the hillside and pine grove stretch between the cloud-set buildings and the valley below; the buildings reveal only emerged roof and eaves, indicating their position in a distant layer separated by cloud and slope | Lower-center valley: a procession of carts, horses, and banners fills the valley passage, and is cut off from the upper-left cloud-set buildings by slope and cloud, with no visible linkage such as bridge or path
distinction: The compositional role of the buildings lies in the layer of concealment and revelation formed by cloud obscuring their base while revealing the roof and eaves, rather than identifying a single scenic spot at the peak edge or valley mouth

evidence: Middle-right waterside: the roofs and walls of several houses are clearly visible; they sit on a level slope by the water with dense trees on the slope behind, and the buildings spread laterally following the shoreline | Center midground foot of the mountain: a group of buildings is distributed along the mountain foot where it meets the mist, rising and falling with the undulations of the foot and corresponding to the turns of the mountain form | Lower-left foreground: the ridge of a thatched roof emerges among slope rocks and tree clumps, sited according to the slope, with the roof orientation tilting with the slope
distinction: The roofs and walls of the houses are clearly exposed, and screening is not the main relationship; their base heights and direction of spread are plainly determined by the bank slope and mountain-foot terrain, so terrain-responsive siting predominates

evidence: Right side, upper-middle to lower-right: multiple storied pavilions and halls are built level upon level on descending terrace bases and platforms; roof heights descend with the hillside, and the retaining walls of the terrace bases correspond one-to-one with the slope forms | Center-left: a group of buildings stands on a waterside terrace base with railings; the platform extends toward the water, and the complex is arranged with its back to the mountain and face to the water, spreading along the bank | Lower left and lower right: on the lower left a railed zigzag bridge has pedestrians walking to the right, and on the lower right a pale stepped path climbs from the slope foot to the platform before the pavilion with figures ascending, forming cues of accessibility
distinction: The layered terrace bases and the waterside spread run through the right half and determine the overall layout of the complex; although the bridge and stepped path are visible, their mid-section linkage is cut off by trees and rocks, subordinating them to the structure of terrain-responsive siting

evidence: Right half: the bank slope descends level by level from beneath the great tree at the upper right; the slope foot and clumps of grass and shrubs form a winding shoreline meeting the open water on the left | Left half and lower-edge water surface: several oxen lie in or ford the water, a herd boy stands on an ox's back, and the motifs are distributed close to the water's edge | Lower-center to lower-right slope foot: the herd and herd boy are placed according to the height of the slope foot, unfolding in order from the water through the water's edge onto the bank, their positions undulating with the bank forms
distinction: The terrain-responsive spread of the motifs along the slope foot and waterside runs through the whole painting, and is closer to the visible spatial organization than the local screening of the oxen by the bank's trees and rocks

evidence: Middle of the right bank, among the trees: behind tree trunks and dense foliage, a small patch of white wall and a corner of a roof is exposed, partly cut off by branches and trunks, suggesting that the house is hidden within the woods | Lower part of the painting, on the sloping bank: the sloping bank extends from lower left to upper right, with a band of trees continuous along it; a corner of the house is just within the screening of the tree belt, forming a foreground-background layering with the distant screen-like peaks | Lower left at the water's edge: a boat with mast and sail mat is moored at the bank, close against the sloping shore, but no path or porch connecting to the woodland house is visible
distinction: The house is shown only by a corner of wall partly cut off by trees, and this concealment-and-revelation relationship constitutes its main mode of presentation; no correspondence between the building site, layout, and the sloping terrain can be seen in the painting, so terrain-responsive siting is not adopted

evidence: Left-center ridge: a storied pavilion-type structure reveals multiple eaves and an upper columned gallery, its lower part screened by rows of trees on the ridge | Left ridge line: a row of trees is arranged diagonally along the ridge, their crowns reaching about the middle of the structure, with the roof emerging from the tree line to form a layer of house seen behind woodland | Center and lower part of the painting: two giant peaks flank an open water surface; a figure stands on a reef in the water, and no bridge, path, gate, gallery, or other movement cues linking to the structure are visible
distinction: The building base is obscured by woodland and invisible; the visible relationship is the layer of concealment and revelation in which roof and eaves emerge from behind the treetops, not a correspondence between base layout and slope-terrace terrain

evidence: Center: two figures stand on a winding bank slope, facing each other, as if meeting on the way or pausing | Lower left to center: the outline of the bank, drawn in pale ink, winds upward from foreground to midground, forming a path direction that can be reached on foot and continued onward | Right and left: withered trees and shrub clumps flank the bank on both sides, and mist and unpainted space provide transition in the distance; no roofs, walls, bridges, gates, or other built elements appear anywhere in the painting
distinction: The painting expresses the process of being reachable and turning into the depths through the direction of the slope path and the standing/walking figures, yet there are no house eaves or walls revealed from behind woodland screening, so concealment and revelation does not hold

evidence: Center-left: a clump of bamboo rises from the slope, its stems and leaves rendered in dense ink; the slope at its base is surrounded by pale mist, and the lower half of the bamboo fades into the misty white | Center-right: a group of flat-topped slope rocks spreads out behind and to the right of the bamboo clump, with only the top surface and front edge clear and the lower part submerged in cloud, presenting a half-revealed state | Upper part and distance: multiple layers of mountain shadows and tree clumps are rendered in pale ink, separated and obscured by horizontal cloud bands, with near-far layering presented through concealment and revelation; no traces of buildings, eaves, walls, bridges, or paths appear throughout
distinction: The layers of the painting are organized mainly by cloud and mist and woodland obscuring and revealing the slope rocks, approaching a concealment-and-revelation relationship; yet the bridge, path, gate, and other accessible cues required by C4 are entirely invisible in the painting

evidence: Upper-middle to right: a railing with carved-panel balusters and posts extends diagonally from the upper left, turning at the middle into a horizontal run on the right; beyond the railing at the upper right white geese float on the water and a stone-revetted bank is visible, and the railing encloses and unfolds along the pond edge | Center: a tree trunk stands at the turn of the railing; the panels and posts are clearly distinguishable, the built components fully exposed, and their course follows the turns of the site rather than being hidden by scenery | Inside the railing on the right bank: a group of figures playing music and unrolling scrolls gathers on the level ground within the railing, with the water immediately outside, showing that the ground enclosed by this section of railing is set at the waterside
distinction: The railing enclosing and unfolding along the pond edge, corresponding to the turns of the shoreline, is the main relationship; the tree trunk only partially screens the railing and does not form a scenic mode in which concealment and revelation indicate built layers

evidence: Upper part of the painting: pine branches hang down from the top edge, and a scaly-textured pine trunk crosses diagonally between the figures, casting cover and local screening over the scene below | Center: four scarf-wearing figures surround a large table, on which are placed utensils and scroll-like objects; no buildings, pavilions, or walls appear | Lower left: beside the table is placed armchair-like furniture with armrests; the painting has no mountains and rocks, waterside, bridges, paths, or other landscape-space elements
distinction: The only natural-scenery organization in the painting is the shade and screening, and revelation, of the pine branches and trunk over the scene, closer to a concealment-and-revelation layer; there are no terrain siting, scenic markers, or movement-access cues to compare with

evidence: Center: the foot of the main peak is cut off by a horizontal mist band, with only the summit and the tree clumps on the ridge revealed, forming an upper-lower layer of concealment and revelation | Midground center-right: between the tree clumps and slope mounds below the mist band are extremely faint horizontal ink patches and short lines, suspected to be roof ridges or eaves, but the details are unclear and cannot be reliably identified | Lower-center to lower-right: unpainted water and the bank's pine grove half-screen the depths of the midground, with ridge and treetops partly emerging from the mist
distinction: The dominant relationship in the painting is the concealment-and-revelation layer of woodland and mist half-screening, rather than a movement process organized by identifiable access cues such as bridges, paths, or fords

evidence: Upper right: a double-eaved storied pavilion stands on a terrace base and enclosure wall atop a cliff, its base rising with the cliff and corresponding to the high-ground form | Center-left: an open pavilion is placed at the edge of a clifftop platform, below which is a steep cliff face, the pavilion's base sited according to the slope terrace | Center: an arch-gate-type structure is embedded in a hollow flanked by two mountains, its base descending with the slope and corresponding to the opening and closing of the mountain hollow
distinction: Although there is a bridge at the lower right and a gate opening at the center, the movement cues lack continuous, identifiable entry linkage with the built structures, whereas the correspondence of multiple building bases with cliff terraces and mountain hollows runs more directly through the composition

evidence: Lower right: a waterside double-eaved storied pavilion stands on a white terrace platform, with tiered steps in front connecting upward from the waterside; two or three figures stand on the platform, presenting an entry relationship of ascending from the bank to the pavilion | Center to upper-center valley: a red stream valley runs through the painting from bottom to top; terrace bases and buildings advance level by level along the banks, and the upper pavilions emerge layer by layer amid the gaps of peaks and cloud, forming an extending cue of turning into the depths | Center-left: halls and galleries are enclosed between the bank slopes, with the canopy in front screening part of them; their terrace bases connect above and below with the lower waterside terrace base, constituting a link along the valley ascent
distinction: The steps, platforms, and valley shoreline string the groups of buildings into a movement process that can be ascended and entered deeply; the terrain correspondence of base and bank is only the background of this process, not its dominant organization

evidence: Middle of the painting: dense pine branches extend horizontally from the rocky slope on the right, spreading over the top of the pavilion and screening the corner of its right rear eaves, while the front columns and railing of the pavilion emerge from beneath the pine shade | Lower center-right: the open pavilion sits on a masonry terrace base built following the diagonal of the bank slope, backed by the rocky slope on the right, the pavilion set among the roots of the pine grove | Left and upper left: the pavilion faces a large expanse of unpainted water and distant peak walls to the left, with the pine grove and rocky slope forming an enclosing layer behind and above the pavilion
distinction: The presentation of the pavilion is organized mainly by the screening-and-revelation layer of the pine grove and rocky slope, and concealment and revelation runs through the central composition; although the slope-following terrace base is visible, it is a local base treatment and explains less than the concealment-and-revelation relationship

evidence: Lower left: a figure in a straw cape and hat stands barefoot at the edge of shallow water, holding a long staff pointing to the front right, in a posture of walking while looking back, with the bank line at his feet extending diagonally from lower left to right. | Right to center: the bank slope rises diagonally from the lower right; withered trees grow among the great rocks at the top of the bank, one leaning across the middle of the painting and one rising straight to the upper right, leaving a passable gap between the rocks and branches. | Upper left: a waterfall drops from the cliff edge, its lower section partly screened by the leaning withered branches; between the waterfall's base and the bank where the figure stands is open water, and the figure's movement is directed toward the depths below the rocks and waterfall.
distinction: Concealment and revelation in the painting occurs only between the withered branches and the waterfall and does not indicate the presence of any built structure; whereas the figure wading with a staff, the diagonally extending shoreline, and the orientation toward the rock gap constitute the only identifiable movement-and-arrival direction, so C4 predominates.

evidence: Lower left: a traveler in a straw cape and hat stands barefoot on the bank slope, holding a long staff pointing forward, his body facing the rocks and misty white unpainted area on the right side of the painting, in a forward-moving posture | Center to right: the bank slope extends from lower left to upper right, meeting coiled pine roots and layered rocks; gaps and unpainted space remain between the rocks and behind the pine trunks, forming a tendency to continue turning into the depths | Upper-center to left: a cliff wall runs diagonally across the whole painting, and a waterfall drops from a cliff crevice, partly screened by leaning pine branches; no traces of houses, pavilions, bridges, galleries, or other built structures appear throughout
distinction: The dominant relationship is the traveler with staff advancing along the bank while the bank and rocky-gap unpainted space suggest a process of continuing deeper; the house eaves and concealment-revelation required by C2 are entirely absent, and the pine-and-rock screening acts only on the waterfall, not on built structures

evidence: Lower half, center to lower right: a pale stream winds upward from the lower edge of the painting, threading through gaps in the pine grove and disappearing behind the grove at the midground; the shoreline is continuous, forming a cue of deepening that can be followed | Lower-middle clearing in the grove: pine trunks and rounded canopies overlap and screen the bank slope; at the open clearing among the trees a bank rock by the stream is revealed, on which a seated figure plays the qin, while another standing figure to the left is half-screened behind a tree trunk | Whole painting: apart from slope rocks, pine grove, stream, and distant peaks, no traces of houses, pavilions, walls, bridge galleries, or other built structures appear
distinction: The dominant cue is the process of deepening constituted by the winding stream banks, whereas what the pine grove's screening conceals and reveals is figures and slope rocks rather than house roofs, so the concealment explanation is weaker.

evidence: Right half to center: several withered trees stand in staggered front-back order on the bank slope, their trunks, twig clusters, and shrubs screening one another, and the slope foot and the gentle slope behind it appear and disappear through the tree gaps, forming a front-back layer of concealment and revelation. | Lower center to lower left: an islet and clump grass half-screen a flock of resting birds, the islet's shoreline intermittently visible behind the grass, and the water surface opening out from the right bank toward the left. | Whole painting: no houses, eaves, or walls are visible, nor are there bridges, paths, gates, fords, or other movement cues; the painting consists of bank slopes, rock walls, cold woodland, water surface, and flying birds.
distinction: The visible organization is dominated by the screening and concealment/revelation of trees, rocks, and clump grass, and what is concealed and revealed is the bank and islet; the base-terrain correspondence required by C1 has no locus anywhere in the painting, so the concealment-and-revelation layer is closer to the visible relationship.

evidence: Lower right foreground: a conical-roofed thatched pavilion stands on a level, projecting slope platform at the waterside; the pavilion columns and the edge of the terrace base are clear, and the base turns with the shoreline and extends toward the water | Foreground bank slope: the pavilion base is sited on a level spot among layered slope rocks; the slope rocks and tree clumps on the left are slightly higher than the pavilion, which faces the open water of the midground, its height corresponding to the slope form | Midground water surface: between the foreground pavilion terrace and the midground shoreline is open water, and no bridge, path, gate, or ferry links to the pavilion
distinction: The pavilion's base correspondence with the waterside slope platform is clear and organizes the foreground siting relationship, explaining the visible evidence better than its role as a marker identifying a scenic spot

evidence: Right side: the roof, eaves, and columned railing of a storied pavilion emerge from between pine branches and bamboo clumps; the bamboo behind the building rises above the ridge line, and the lower left of the building itself is partly screened by pine branches and bamboo leaves | Lower-edge center: a thatched-roof pavilion is half-screened among slope rocks, pine branches, and bamboo leaves, revealing only the roof and a small amount of framework | Center to right: a giant pine coils upward from the right slope, its branches spreading across in front of the pavilion, placing the pavilion in a spatial layer behind the woodland
distinction: Although the pavilion sits on the slope top, the painting organizes its appearance through the screening and revelation of pine branches and bamboo clumps, and the concealment-and-revelation layer runs through the composition more than the correspondence of base and slope surface

evidence: Among the slope rocks below: four figures pause on the foreground bank: three sit or lean behind rocks with only their upper bodies showing, and one stands at the lower left holding a long strip-like object; the figures have all arrived here and look up toward the pine and waterfall above | Center to upper part: a pine tree leans out from the lower-right slope rocks and crosses the midground; above it a waterfall pours down through a mountain gap, and mist separates the midground from the distant mountains, forming a space that advances from foreground to depths | Lower ground: the foreground is gentle sloping ground with gaps between boulders, where one can stand and pass; the midground's unpainted space and a band of pale-ink distant trees suggest water surface and shoreline, helping to indicate that the space extends into the depths
distinction: The main label takes the arrival and continuable spatial process suggested by the figures pausing on the bank and facing the depths of the stream and waterfall; although C2-style pine-and-rock screening exists, there is no revealed built object being concealed and revealed in the painting, so concealment does not become its dominant compositional role

evidence: Center-left: a snow-covered roof and the railed building itself stand behind withered trees and cold woodland, with trunks and branches lying across in front of the house, the building half-revealed through the tree gaps | Center-right: a trellis-type building with a column row is revealed between the snowy slope and rocks at the bank, its roof snow-covered and its rear side screened by slope rocks | Central foreground: a large slope rock and cold trees stretch across the middle of the painting, pushing the houses and trellis into a layer behind them, with ridges and eaves emerging through tree gaps and rock edges
distinction: Although the built structures lie in the bank zone, the composition is dominated by the concealment-and-revelation layer in which cold woodland and slope rocks screen the houses while roof ridges and eave columns emerge through forest gaps, and the terrain correspondence is less clear than the concealment relationship

evidence: Lower-right water edge: a thin diagonal line extends from the right bank's slope foot toward the water, with a short dotted vertical structure at its end, resembling a bridge or ferry plank, but the details are unclear and it cannot be confirmed as a built structure or a boat bridge. | Lower bank to middle-right bank: the lower bank and tree group extend to the right along the water edge, meeting the middle-right slope across an unpainted water gap, and the gap between shoreline and water surface forms a passage turning toward the depths of the painting. | Lower-center bank edge: at the slope foot are scattered dot clusters and short vertical lines, suspected to be very small huts or figures, but the ink marks are blurred and cannot be reliably identified.
distinction: The main label relies on the reachable process suggested by the suspected ferry-bridge cue at the water edge and the shoreline extension; the alternative concealment explanation lacks any identifiable roof or eave concealment/revelation.

evidence: Lower left: a horizontally laid-out flat stone slab supports a seated figure, with the qin laid across the stone surface, and the stone slab plays a base-like supporting role in the painting | Upper-middle: a slender branch with white flowers grows from behind the stone slab and spreads upward, forming a front-back corresponding arrangement with the slab | Center-right to right: a slender-stemmed broadleaf plant runs vertically through, separating the figure seated with his back turned from the figure on the right; no houses, pavilions, galleries, bridges, paths, or other built components appear in the whole painting
distinction: Although flowers and trees form a front-back layer with the stone slab, there are no roofs, walls, or other built components revealed after being screened; the base-like placement of the seated figure and qin on the slab is the only identifiable terrain-responsive arrangement correspondence in the painting, so C1 rather than C2 is adopted.

evidence: Upper-right ridge: a multi-storied finial emerges from behind the ridge and pine grove, the lower section of the pagoda body obscured by the mountain, with only several upper tiers and the spire visible | Lower left: the pitched roofs of several houses emerge above the dense treetops, most of the building bodies hidden behind the woodland | Lower right: a group of white-walled houses is half-screened between the bank and cloud, with a small bridge on the stream bank in front, but no clear path linkage between the bridge and the houses is visible
distinction: Although the small stream-bank bridge is visible, its linkage with the built structures and subsequent movement cues is unclear; whereas the pagoda finial and roofs all emerge partially by means of screening by ridge and woodland to indicate spatial layers, and the concealment-and-revelation relationship runs through the upper, middle, and lower sections of the composition

evidence: Lower section of the painted panel, slightly left: behind and to the left of a dense-ink grove, a roof and eave lines drawn in pale ink are exposed, the building itself partly screened by the grove and the slope surface | Among the horizontal-dot woodland below the cloud band in the middle section of the painted panel: a faint inverted-V roof ridge emerges at the edge of the woodland, in a layer behind the cloud and smoke and the tree dots | Water at the lower right of the painted panel: only a small boat rests on the water, and no entry clues such as bridges, paths or gates connecting with the houses are seen
distinction: The correspondence between the houses and the sloping-bank terrain is vague, whereas the layering of concealment and revelation, in which their roofs are half-exposed from the grove and the cloud-and-smoke woodland edge, is clearer and runs through the upper and lower sections of the composition.

evidence: Lower center-left: a zigzag enclosure wall extends from the left edge to the middle of the painting, its end joining a roofed gatehouse; the gate opening is open, a figure stands within, and a terrace base and steps are in front of the gate | Lower right: a red-robed rider and walking attendants travel along a level path below the cliff, and a section of arched-bridge railing appears at the lower-right edge; the path seems to continue from the bridge and approach toward the gate and wall | Center-right: behind coiled pine branches and tree clumps, roof eaves, flat-deck railings, and a pointed pavilion ridge are revealed, located on the cliff slope above and behind the space enclosed by the gate and wall
distinction: The bridge, path, gate, and wall form a continuous movement cue of arriving from outside and turning into the courtyard, and the figures' advance reinforces the entry process; concealment and revelation only explain the local screening and revealing of the building behind the trees and cannot explain the organizing role of the wall gate and travel in the composition

evidence: Middle to right side of the painting: multiple groups of pavilions and halls descend in tiers from upper left to lower right along the ridge and slope platforms, with building heights corresponding to the direction of the mountain terrain, presenting a layout of separate placement according to the slope | Slightly left of center: below the pavilions, fine columns can be seen supporting on the cliff slope, with the building base erected following the slope, showing that the built elements are placed according to the terrain | Lower right middle: tiers of pavilions stand at the slope foot and waterside, a white balustraded platform connects the upper and lower buildings, trees intersperse among them but the outline of the building group is clear
distinction: Although trees partially screen the eaves and wall bodies, the building group as a whole is exposed and its tiered order is determined by the height of the slope platforms; concealment and revelation is not the main means of organizing space

evidence: Lower center, behind the withered tree: a round-canopied shelter-like object (possibly a boat awning or thatched hut) emerges from behind the trunk and branches of the withered tree, its top surface bearing fine vertical striations, its lower part obscured by the tree body and the grass on the bank | Among the branches to the right of the central withered tree: a vertical line-frame structure with crossbars is visible, possibly a fence, brushwood gate, or fishing gear, adjacent to the shelter-like object behind the tree, details unclear | Lower left to lower center bank slope: the bank slope and the slanting withered tree form a foreground screen; the shelter-like object and the boat-shaped horizontal lines to its right rest on the water at the bank side, forming a layering of concealment and revelation from front to back
distinction: The painting is dominated by the layering of a roof revealed from behind trees; no identifiable entry clues such as bridges, paths, gates, or crossings, nor built-element connections, are seen, hence concealment and revelation rather than access to secluded settings

evidence: Upper right to right center mountain hollow and ridge: multiple groups of buildings are arranged in tiers along slope platforms, building heights rising and falling with the undulations of the ridge, building bases set on the gentle ground of the mountain hollow | Valley between the two mountains at left center: a group of buildings is placed on the sloped bank of the valley, the roof faces toward the open side of the valley, corresponding with the enclosing hillside | Slope foot in the lower part of the painting: thatched huts are placed in a clearing among trees at the slope foot, the base set according to the slope platform, with no arrangement independent of the terrain visible
distinction: Although clumps of trees surround the buildings, the roofs and wall bodies are mostly fully exposed on the open slope platforms; the relationship running through the whole painting is the correspondence between the rising and falling deployment of built elements and the mountain terrain and slope platforms, rather than organizing layers through screening and exposure

evidence: Right center: several buildings spread horizontally along the slope platforms at the mountain foot, their undersides supported on the slope surface by rows of posts, roof ridges rising and falling with the terrain | Right of center: the building group backs onto the slope of the right foot of the main ridge, facing the open area below, the base corresponding with the mountain form and slope | Lower center to right: two ox carts and drivers travel along the flat ground at the mountain foot, with no visible path, bridge, or gate connecting their route to the buildings on the right
distinction: The buildings are placed with posts following the height of the slope platforms, their relation of backing onto the mountain and facing the water being clear and running through the middle ground, while the foreground cart route lacks identifiable entry connections to the buildings; hence terrain-responsive siting is closer to the visible relations than access to secluded settings

evidence: Lower center to lower right: several figures carrying loads on shoulder poles and boxes and cages form a line walking on the flat ground between slopes, moving in the same direction, presenting a process of movement through the landscape from here to there | Center of the middle ground: a flat opening is left between the sloped bank and the pile of blue-green rocks, the ground extending toward the depth of the painting, continuing the direction of the figures' movement | Whole painting: apart from huge pines, withered trees, and slope rocks, no traces of buildings, pavilions, bridges, gates, or other built elements are seen, nor any concealed or revealed roofs or wall bodies
distinction: The only prominent spatial organization in the painting is the traversable process of the figure procession moving along the opening in the slope; the relations of built-element placement, concealment and revelation, or scenic accentuation required by C1–C3 have no visible counterparts

evidence: Lower right slope platform: two sections of balustrade with posts are set at the water's edge of the slope platform; one person leans on the railing, one stands gazing upward, and an attendant carrying objects stands behind the railing, the balustraded platform facing the churning water outlet below | Upper left to middle of the composition: a waterfall drops from between high cliffs straight down to the torrent at the lower end of the painting, facing the lower-right balustraded platform across the water, forming a diagonal echo | Above and behind the lower-right balustraded platform: bamboo clumps and slope rocks rise from behind the platform, framing the open side of the platform facing the waterfall mouth, making this spot the focal point of sightlines in the whole painting
distinction: Although the balustraded platform is set according to the slope platform, its compositional role lies mainly in facing the waterfall mouth and concentrating the scene of waterfall viewing; the terrain correspondence serves to identify the waterside scene rather than to emphasize placement following the terrain

evidence: Upper left to left bank: a withered tree extends from the top of the snow-covered bank, its branches slanting across and covering the upper part of the painting, string-like ornaments hanging at the side of the branches; no buildings, eaves, walls, or other built elements are seen | Center to center right: the snow slope extends and undulates from the left bank to the right, the slope surface open and empty, with no bridges, paths, gates, corridors, or other movement clues | Lower middle slope foot: three figures and a sheep are placed in a hollow at the slope foot, backing onto the snow slope and facing outward from the slope, one person holding a long pole pointing diagonally toward the side of the tree on the left bank
distinction: The main subject of the painting is placed in the hollow at the slope foot with its back to the slope; the relation of the bank terrain participating in the placement runs through the composition more than the layering of concealment by the withered branches covering the top

evidence: Among the waterside rocks at lower center: between the outlined slope rocks and grass there is a dark blue-gray block-like object and a horizontal wood-like member, possibly part of a building or shed frame, most of which is obscured by foreground rocks and vegetation, details unclear | Lower right bank: a figure sits on a slope rock facing the open water to the left, bamboo clumps and slanting branches behind screening the space behind the slope, forming a layering of foreground figure and background bamboo | Upper half of the composition: pine branches slant down from the upper right covering the upper blank, forming with the lower bank and the unpainted water surface two spatial layers, upper and lower, the large unpainted area in the middle serving as water surface or cloud vapor
distinction: The suspected built structure is revealed in part, half-hidden by the waterside rocks and vegetation; concealment and revelation is its only identifiable compositional role; the painting shows no clear evidence of building base, building itself, or placement corresponding to terrain height, hence C1 is not adopted.

evidence: Upper part to upper middle: buildings are erected on a diagonally brick-paved platform, the platform edge fitted with red railings that turn with the platform edge, the tables and figures inside the buildings on the open side, presenting buildings set according to the platform | Middle: a curtained canopy is attached to the lower edge of the platform, its posts standing near the platform edge; the group of children and tables beneath the canopy are on a platform lower than the upper buildings, forming separate placement according to platform height | Lower left and lower right: at lower left a sumeru-style pedestal supports the trunk of a large tree; at lower right railings enclose the lower platform edge with a stone table, the pedestals and railings marking the layered courtyard terraces and participating in the high-low organization of building bases
distinction: Although pine branches, plum branches, and banana leaves sweep past the fronts of the buildings and the canopy top, the buildings and canopy are clearly and completely exposed; concealment and revelation does not dominate the composition; what runs through the composition is the correspondence of buildings, canopy, and railings placed according to the height of the terraces

evidence: Upper part to right bank: reeds, bamboo clumps, and tree trunks hang down from the bank, their branches and leaves overlapping and screening the slope rocks and the space behind them, forming a clear layering of concealment and revelation | Open ground in the middle of the composition: on the unpainted flat slope only one large and one small ox are seen, with no traces of buildings, wall bodies, eaves, or other built elements at all | Lower part: earth slopes and grass undulate, the slope opening facing the middle-ground clearing, with no building bases, bridges, paths, gates, crossings, or other artificial clues seen
distinction: The identifiable spatial layering in the painting comes from the screening and exposure of the bank by vegetation, not from the corresponding placement of terrain and building bases, hence C2 rather than C1.

evidence: Upper left to center: a thick pine trunk slants out from a gap in the cliff on the left, its branches extending horizontally to the right following the cliff's momentum, the pine needles hanging in clusters in the air, the direction of extension corresponding with the trend of the cliff face | Lower left to lower center: slope rocks pile up in layers, with bamboo clumps and moss dots between them supporting the pines and rocks above; no traces of buildings, walls, eaves, bridges, paths, or other built elements are seen in the whole composition | Left center: a pale winding band descends along the cliff face in twists to the slope foot, resembling a stream trace or rock crevice, not connecting with any identifiable built element
distinction: The visible organization consists mainly of pines and rocks extending following the cliff's momentum and supported at the slope foot, i.e. placement according to terrain, rather than using concealment and revelation to suggest the layering of buildings, hence C1 is taken as the closest classification

evidence: Lower center of the painting: a row of balustrades with posts extends diagonally along the sloped bank, stepped slope rocks visible below the railing, forming a walkable passage of a bridge or plank road | Lower left to lower center: a figure wearing a conical hat and cloak rides a horse to the left, two attendants walking behind, the figures' movement connecting with the railing path below, presenting a process of traveling along the path and continuing forward | Among the trees at center right: behind hanging branches and shrubs is a row of fine vertical line-like structures, possibly a fence or curtain, but details unclear and not reliably identifiable as buildings
distinction: The dominant relation in the painting is the traversable, continuable process of movement formed by the railing path, mountain path, and traveling figures; at center right there is only one vague suspected structure, and the layering of concealment and revelation is insufficient to dominate the composition

evidence: Slightly left of center: a large lake rock rises, chrysanthemums and branches and leaves extending from the top and sides of the rock, the rock body screening the space behind it, forming a layering of screening front and back | Lower center: two water birds stand among white flowers, their bodies partly screened by flowers and leaves, only heads, backs, and tail feathers exposed, the relation of concealment and revelation running through the flower clump | Bottom: grass blades sweep and water ripples are seen, presenting a waterside slope; no traces of buildings, walls, bridges, paths, gates, or other built elements are seen in the whole composition
distinction: The dominant relation in the painting is the layering of screening and exposure of the scenery by flowers and rocks, rather than the corresponding placement of built elements with slope platforms and waterside, for which there is no visible evidence at all

evidence: Center: a gentlewoman sits in a spot enclosed by lake rocks, lake rocks and hanging banana leaves behind and on both sides, her figure revealed through the gaps between banana leaves and rocks. | Lower left: several figures gather beneath slope rocks and banana trunks, one of them with only the head revealed from behind a slope rock, forming a layering of concealment behind the rock. | Lower right: a gentlewoman sits on a legged seat, a long case placed in front, below which a group of lake rocks screens, forming a front-back layering with the group of figures at lower left.
distinction: Although the seated spot is adjacent to slope rocks, the painting more prominently highlights the layering of partial screening of figures and the seated spot by banana leaves and lake rocks; the relation of concealment and revelation runs through the composition more than the correspondence of base placement following the form.

evidence: Right center: the roof ridge, eaves, and beam frame of an open pavilion are revealed through gaps in the dense tree canopy, the upper part of the roof screened by hanging branches and leaves | Right of center, in front of the pavilion: a large rock and slanting pine branches in front of the pavilion block the lower half of the building, the columns and figures inside revealed from behind the rock and among the trees, forming a layering of seeing the building through a screen | Lower middle slope: two attendants and a donkey stand among the slope rocks; no bridges, paths, gates, corridors, or other identifiable movement clues connecting with the open pavilion are seen on the slope
distinction: Although the figures and donkey stand in front of the pavilion suggesting arrival, no visible entry clues such as bridges, paths, gates, or corridors exist; the relation of concealment and revelation by which the roof and eave columns are screened by trees and rocks directly organizes the presentation of the building, hence C2 is primary

evidence: Slightly right of the center of the painting: building outlines drawn in pale ink reveal overlapping roofs, the lower half of the buildings submerged in the dense, horizontally spreading tree canopy below, only the eave tops visible | Lower center of the painting: between the slope and the trees, the roof and eave columns of buildings are outlined in pale lines, the left side of the buildings adjacent to a large area of foreground tree shadow, in a half-hidden state | Around the central buildings: the buildings lie in the hollow between two ridges on the left and right, flanked by ridges and tree clumps, not occupying an independent and prominent peak-edge or water-outlet position
distinction: The correspondence between building bases and slope platforms is obscured by tree shadows and dim ink tones and is unclear; the visible relation is mainly the layering of concealment and revelation of roofs revealed among forest ridges, hence C2 rather than C1 placement according to the slope

evidence: Upper left: a human face is revealed between a slanting thick tree trunk and a rock crevice, the body screened by the trunk and rock wall, only the head, shoulders, and part of the scaly lower body visible | Right side: behind hanging pine branches and pine-needle clusters, several faces and limbs are revealed, part of the bodies hidden behind pine branches and rock walls, forming a front-back layering of concealment and revelation | Center: a waterfall pours down from the cliff mouth, a crowd of running figures overlapping among the waterfall, fallen trees, and slope rocks, their legs and feet cut off by rocks and wood, objects arranged in layers by screening and exposure
distinction: The painting organizes spatial layers by the screening and exposure of objects by trees and rocks, rather than connecting spaces with traversable clues such as bridges, paths, gates, or crossings; hence the relation of concealment and revelation is closer to the visible organization than the process of movement

evidence: Among the trees on the left-center sloped bank: a gabled roof and eaves are revealed through dense branches and leaves, the building itself screened by the trees, only the revealed roof indicating the existence of the building and its level | Among the cliffs at upper right: pavilions and railings are placed in a recess of the cliff, their lower part half-screened by the trees and rock wall in front, presenting a spatial layering of seeing buildings behind rocks | Water surface at center right: a wooden plank bridge crosses the water, two people with staffs walking on it, the bridge's two ends resting on an islet and the right bank slope, not directly connecting with visible buildings
distinction: Although the movement clue on the bridge is clear, the bridge ends stop at the sloped bank and do not connect with the built elements, so the entry process does not point to the buildings; the two building locations both use tree and rock screening and exposure to indicate their existence and level, and the relation of concealment and revelation more directly organizes the built elements

evidence: Wide water surface from the center to the lower part of the whole composition: ripple-patterned water spreads diagonally across the composition, many figures in white wade in a line, continuing from upper right to lower left, forming a movement clue from here to there | Upper right: a rocky bank extends into the water, on the bank platform are seated and standing figures, connecting with the water surface, forming the bank on one side of the crossing | Lower left: several figures gather at the foot of the rocks, directly connecting with the water surface, forming the other bank where the line arrives
distinction: The painting is dominated by the process of crossing the water, with the wading procession connecting the rocks of the two banks, rather than built elements placed according to the banks; since the whole painting has no built elements, C4 is adopted only as the closest classification to the visible spatial organization

evidence: Diagonal bank from center to upper right: the slope surface extends diagonally from lower left to upper right, fine grass growing on the ridge and foot of the slope, forming the main spatial division and directional trend of the painting | Lower left and left center: spiral water patterns turn and unfold in layers along the edge of the bank, suggesting the site relation of waterside and slope platforms | Whole painting: apart from flying birds, grassy slopes, water patterns, and rocks in the lower-left corner, no traces of buildings, walls, bridges, paths, gates, or any other built elements are seen
distinction: The only identifiable spatial organization in the painting is the correspondence between the sloped bank and the waterside terrain, with no movement clues such as bridges, paths, gates, or crossings connecting them, hence C4 is not adopted and only terrain organization is used for the closest C1 classification

evidence: Lower left: the roof, eaves, and windowed wall body of a thatched hut are revealed from behind foreground slope rocks and trees, the right side of the building cut off by slope trees | Lower center: several large trees with dense shade and withered branches on the earth slope lie between the viewer and the buildings, the canopy and slope body forming a screening layer in front of the buildings | Lower right water surface: an empty boat is moored at the bank at the slope foot, with no visible bridges, paths, or gates connecting it to the buildings
distinction: The buildings are mainly revealed by the screening of slope rocks and dense trees, exposing roof and wall bodies to indicate their existence and level, the relation of concealment and revelation being prominent; the corresponding arrangement of base and terrain is not obvious, hence C1 is not adopted

evidence: Lower right: a person carrying a long object walks on a bridge path with posts and horizontal railings, body facing the center of the painting, presenting movement dynamics | Slightly below center: two scholars stand on open flat ground, which connects on the right with the approaching bridge path and on the left with the platform in front of the buildings, the ground continuous and passable | Left center: behind the pine trees are revealed the eaves, columns, and railing panels of an open pavilion, a seated figure visible inside, the platform in front of the pavilion connecting with the central flat ground, forming the destination of the movement
distinction: The bridge path, traveler, and open ground in front of the buildings form an identifiable sequence of entry and convergence, organizing the lower half of the painting throughout; although pine branches screen the buildings to form layers, the buildings are clearly and completely exposed, and concealment and revelation is not the dominant device

evidence: Lower part, slightly left: a plank bridge crosses a stream, on the bridge one person rides a horse and one walks following, on the right bank of the bridge other travelers and horses move along the stream bank into the mountains | Middle mountain hollow: monastery pavilions and red-walled halls are placed on the open ground of the hollow, several small standing figures on the flat ground in front of the monastery, presenting gathering after arrival | Lower center to center: the stream and springs and the gaps among rocks extend upward from the lower shoreline to the open ground in front of the monastery, the bridge, shoreline, and figures before the monastery forming a sequence from outside to inside, the middle section of the path partly cut off by rocks
distinction: The bridge and travel clues run through the lower half of the painting and point toward the monastery in the mountain hollow, organizing a process of arrival and possible further penetration; concealment and revelation only explains the local screening of roofs by forest and rock, and is less explanatory than the movement sequence

evidence: Upper left: the roof, eaves, and flat-platform railings of pavilions drawn in pale ink lines are revealed from behind cloud heads and rocks, the lower part of the buildings cut off by cloud vapor | Left center to center: a group of figures holding musical instruments and ceremonial regalia walk above the cloud vapor, separated from the upper-left pavilions by cloud and mist, with no bridges, paths, gates, or other connections seen | Center to right: rocks, waterfalls, and large areas of cloud vapor occupy the main body of the painting, buildings occupying only a corner at upper left, indicating their spatial level by concealment and revelation
distinction: The procession above the clouds forms no reachable entry connection with the buildings; the existence of the buildings is mainly indicated by cloud and rock screening and revelation, hence concealment and revelation rather than access to secluded settings

evidence: Lower right waterside: a white-walled open pavilion is set by the water, its eaves and roof partly covered by the slanting red-leaf tree trunk and branches in the foreground, the wall body, columns, and figures inside revealed from behind the tree | Left-center mountain-foot forest edge: several roof ridges are revealed from among tree clumps and cloud mist, the building bodies hidden, presenting a deeper level of seeing buildings in the forest | Above the lower-right hall and at its left end: pine branches and mixed tree branches and leaves hang over the hall roof, the left end of the hall screened by tree clumps, only the right section of white wall and the open pavilion clearly visible
distinction: Although the boat and the load-carriers face the waterside hall, no identifiable entry connections such as bridges, paths, or ferry crossings are seen; the dominant relation running through foreground and middle ground is the layering of concealment and revelation formed by trees screening the buildings

evidence: Right-center lower part of the painting: the roofs and eaves of two groups of buildings are revealed above dense horizontal-dot tree clumps, the lower wall bodies and building bases screened by trees, presenting a layering of seeing buildings in the forest | Center: the main peak rises high in the center, the buildings located among trees at the forested foot of the slope to the lower right of the main peak, half-screened by multiple layers of trees front and back | Lower part, slightly left: a figure stands on the sloped bank facing the waterfall, with no identifiable movement connections such as bridges, paths, or gates between it and the buildings
distinction: The buildings are mainly indicated in their level of existence by the relation of concealment and revelation of tree screening and roof exposure, rather than by the corresponding placement of base, layout, and slope platform and waterside terrain

evidence: Center right, slightly low: an arc-shaped mat-patterned canopy top is revealed from among reeds and grass, the lower part of the shelter screened by grass, only the top surface and eave edge visible, suggesting built elements hidden behind grass and trees | Center right: two people stand at the edge of the platform in front of the shelter, the horizontal line of the platform extending toward beneath the shelter, the built element surrounded by clumps of grass and reeds, forming a layering of foreground screening and middle-ground roof exposure | Left side to center: weeping willows and tree clumps slant out from the left bank, branches and leaves hanging over the space above the shelter top, together with the mist surface forming a relation of seeing buildings through tree gaps
distinction: The existence of the built element is mainly indicated by the mat-patterned canopy top and eave edge revealed after being screened by grass, concealment and revelation organizing the layers; the level waterside bank is only background, and no evidence is seen of placement dominated by terrain height or shoreline

evidence: Lower left to slightly below center: a gentle earthen bank undulates from left to right, several clumps of bamboo planted on the slope surface, the bases of the stalks distributed in scattered heights following the slope | Lower right: at the end of the bank several more low bamboo clumps grow close to the slope, the slope surface rendered in pale ink; no traces of buildings, eaves, bridges, paths, or other built elements are seen in the whole composition | Upper half of the composition: the upper part of the painting is a large area of unpainted space, only ink bamboo branches and leaves extending toward the void, with no building outline or roof revealed
distinction: The only identifiable placement relation in the painting is the distribution of bamboo clumps following the undulations of the bank, the terrain participating in the arrangement of elements; although the overlapping of bamboo leaves front and back gives a sense of layering, it does not indicate the existence of any screened built element, hence placement according to terrain is a closer classification to the visible organization.

evidence: Upper-right mountain hollow: the roof and eaves of a group of buildings are revealed from a recess in the ridge, the lower part of the building screened by the slope surface and tree clumps, only the upper roof and eave lines clearly discernible | Around the upper-right buildings: sparse forest and withered trees dot the front and back of the buildings, tree tops and roof ridges interlocking, the architecture in a deep level screened by woodland | Water surface below: a canopied boat is moored on the water beside the sloped bank, figures in the boat, but no visible bridges, paths, gates, or other connections between the boat and the upper-right buildings
distinction: The buildings are mainly indicated in their existence and level by the relation of concealment and revelation of roofs revealed through forest gaps and from behind the slope surface, rather than by a clearly discernible correspondence between base height and terrain, hence concealment and revelation is closer to the visible evidence than terrain-responsive siting

evidence: Lower center: a group of withered trees and dense-leaf clusters stand in a recess of slope rocks, the tree roots screened by foreground slope rocks, branches and leaf clusters screening each other | Center: the peak foot and middle-ground slope rocks are half-hidden behind tree canopies and trunks, forming a front-back layering of concealment and revelation | Whole composition: apart from rocks, withered trees, and banks, no clear built elements such as buildings, pavilions, bridges, or paths are seen
